chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
The ʿāqilah does not bear liability for intentional killing, nor for a confession, nor for a settlement.

key_terms.إِقْرَارًا: a confession by the liable person
key_terms.الْعَاقِلَةُ: the male agnatic relatives who bear liability in certain homicide cases

ai.seo_question: When does the ʿāqilah not bear liability in homicide cases according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning liability in homicide cases. It establishes that the ʿāqilah does not bear financial responsibility in cases of intentional killing, when liability is established by confession, or when a settlement has been reached.
